newsitem.title: USA: Leach - banking package before House maybe next week.
newsitem.headline: Leach - banking package before House maybe next week.

text.p: House Banking Committee Chairman Jim Leach said Wednesday compromise legislation he proposed to shore up the thrift industry insurance fund, cut regulatory red tape for banks and modernize the banking system, could go before the House floor as early as next week.

Leach, an Iowa Republican, said Monday when he announced the proposed measure he believed it would win support from key banking and industry groups. Leach pulled the plug on an earlier version after it ran into stiff opposition.
Leach said in a statement Wednesday he had notified Committee members the leadership had agreed to early floor consideration of the legislative package.
Leach said Monday he believed "we are now at a point" where his proposal would have the support of major banking and insurance groups.
He said the proposal, drafted after extensive talks with House Democrats, included legislation approved by his committee this year to shore up the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
It also includes "noncontroversial" elements of earlier legislation aimed at modernizing the banking industry.
The proposal excludes earlier controversial language covering the Community Reinvestment Act and banks' involvement in insurance activities.
To meet objections voiced by Democrats, it scales back earlier proposals to cut regulatory red tape for banks.
Among particular items, the proposal calls for a General Accounting Office study of state supervision of national bank insurance activities.

In addition, the "closely related to banking" test under the Bank Holding Company Act would be changed to a "financial in nature or incidental to such financial activities" test, with an amendment clarifying that "financial in nature" does not mean insurance or annuities.
